original.statement: Waypoints no longer require DNSProxy to be enabled to consume auto-allocated IPs.

exposure.needed: which configuration shows that an environment uses waypoints, relies on auto-allocated IPs, and has DNSProxy disabled (the release note names no key, flag or env var for any of these)

corrected.statement: Waypoints no longer require DNSProxy to be enabled in order to consume auto-allocated IPs. Exposed environments are those that use waypoints with auto-allocated IPs while DNSProxy is not enabled. The evidence names no configuration key for any of these, so exposure cannot be decided statically.

decision.reason: [ev-3cf1259609e1] says only that waypoints needed DNSProxy enabled in order to consume auto-allocated IPs. So the affected environments are those that use waypoints with auto-allocated IPs and do not have DNSProxy enabled. The proposed feature-gate "ambient" condition is not mentioned anywhere in the evidence and is too broad: it would flag every ambient environment, including ones that use no waypoints, no auto-allocation, or that already enable DNSProxy. The evidence names no configuration key, flag or env var for waypoints, auto-allocation or DNSProxy, so the exposure can only be stated as undecidable until that is known.
